expectations.text: Applies the clause test explicitly: every clause must describe something the project has done or will plausibly do this year.
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement of this test appears anywhere in Section 9; omissions are justified individually ("inventing one to fill the template would be fiction") but the general test is never named.

expectations.text: Follows the template section order for the sections it keeps, and skips the ones the project does not need rather than reordering.
expectations.evidence: Document proceeds Scope→Roles→Decisions→Reduced availability→Adding a maintainer→Stepping back→Changing this document, a sensible unreordered progression, with omissions explained in "What's left out, and why".

expectations.text: Lists merge rights separately from privileged credentials such as signing, publishing and organization ownership in the roles section.
expectations.evidence: "Maintainers: Samuel, Nadia. Merge, release, and decide direction." vs. separate "Release keys: both hold npm publish rights and GitHub org admin."

expectations.text: Includes an aging-approval or single-approver rule so that routine changes can still land while one of the two maintainers is away.
expectations.evidence: "If only one maintainer is reachable, a pending change may merge after 7 days with no objection."

expectations.text: Includes a scope sentence stating what the project refuses to become, so that features can be declined impersonally.
expectations.evidence: "It stays a date-formatting library; new scope (i18n backends, a CLI, a plugin system) is out unless both agree."

expectations.text: Includes an inactivity definition in months and an emeritus clause with rights removed, credit retained, and reinstatement stated.
expectations.evidence: "they move to emeritus" and "keeps credit in MAINTAINERS.md; their credentials are rotated" are present, but no reinstatement process is stated anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Includes a named end state: a successor named, or an archive announced publicly, rather than the project going silent.
expectations.evidence: "If both step back with no successor, we archive the repository publicly rather than leave it silently unmaintained."

expectations.text: States that an archive announcement marks the repository read-only, states the last supported version and the security policy, and points at a successor fork if one exists.
expectations.evidence: The archive clause only says "we archive the repository publicly" with no detail on read-only status, last supported version, security policy, or successor fork.

expectations.text: Says explicitly that the project holds no meetings, rather than inventing a meeting cadence.
expectations.evidence: "No meetings section — you don't have standing meetings; inventing one to fill the template would be fiction the first time it's skipped."

expectations.text: Links the neighbouring files (contribution mechanics, code of conduct, people file, security policy) rather than absorbing their content, so that a process tweak is not a governance amendment.
expectations.evidence: Only MAINTAINERS.md is referenced; no CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, or SECURITY.md links appear anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Includes an amendments clause with a threshold and a window, plus a line stating that changing the document is expected rather than a crisis.
expectations.evidence: "Both maintainers agree, in a pull request open at least 7 days" has threshold/window but no line stating amendment is normal/expected rather than a crisis.

expectations.text: Recommends publishing the reduced-availability period, and treats a stated weekly time budget as a legitimate governance clause rather than something to keep quiet about.
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly advises the opposite: "Track the real dates privately (shared calendar, not the repo)" and there is no stated weekly-hours clause anywhere in the document.
